managed_state.bootstrap_target_anchor: sha256(product namespace plus canonical absolute target).lock
managed_state.bootstrap_anchor_publication: complete fsynced temporary marker published with native atomic no-replace rename semantics and no hard-link alias publication; existing anchors are opened no-create/no-follow and never truncated, rebound, or replaced
managed_state.read_only_bootstrap_coordination: successful read commands create no product or canonical target anchor; cold no-anchor reads double-check product-anchor absence and retry if it appears; seeded reads lock the product anchor shared and hand off to a pre-existing canonical target anchor when present
managed_state.cleanup_stage_binding: promotion stage entries bind source_anchor=canonical_target plus bounded relative source_relative, source_parent_identity, and source_kind=cleanup-source-directory to destination_anchor=cleanup_parent plus bounded relative destination_relative, fixed destination parent binding, and destination_kind=cleanup-tombstone-payload-directory; no absolute rename/delete capabilities or broad lookalike adoption are valid
managed_state.cleanup_journal_publication: complete immutable identity-bound pending journal published once with native atomic no-replace rename; a complete durable promotion stage with bounded relative move intent is published before the first source-to-tombstone move; an immutable cleanup drain intent is published before the first recursive tombstone deletion and is retired last; once an exact final journal and tombstones are visible, stage-retirement faults return success with cleanup_pending; read-only commands expose valid pending or draining state without repair and fail closed on temp aliases, standalone or malformed stage residue, missing tombstones without drain intent, nlink mismatch, malformed, unknown, or over-bound pending state
managed_state.cleanup_pending_result: status, plan, software-status, setup lifecycle, and software lifecycle JSON expose top-level cleanup_pending; setup and software lifecycle mutators expose cleanup_drained
managed_state.co_owned_config_strategy: schema-3 config and runtime allowlist are complete managed JSON files; legacy schema-1 co-owned files and schema-2 coupled setup files are readable only for status, migrate, restore, and remove

setup_system.identity_source: official Junie CLI docs and installer scripts from junie.jetbrains.com

full-auto.allowlist: minimal managed allowlist; Brave On carries the permission posture

unsupported.auto: Brave Auto exists in the UI, but no stable config/env schema for selecting it is confirmed.

safety.external_bootstrap_lock_fixed_system_tem: macOS resolved /private/tmp; Linux /tmp; never ambient TMPDIR
safety.lock_file_open_flags: external and internal locks are O_NOFOLLOW regular files with nonblocking fcntl.flock
safety.same_uid_no_sandbox_boundary: The manager blocks ordinary target-local lock rename/unlink replacement through the external bootstrap lock and blocks ordinary unlink/replace inside dedicated protected lock and launch-image directories while it holds path protections, but it is not a sandbox against deliberate same-UID tampering of the fixed bootstrap root or ancestors.

ubuntu_support.desktop_server_model: Ubuntu Desktop and Server share ID=ubuntu plus glibc host detection.

unsupported_platforms.windows: Rejected before target inspection, network, staging, or runtime mutation even though official windows-* artifacts exist.
unsupported_platforms.non-ubuntu-linux: Rejected before network, staging, or runtime mutation even when an official linux-* artifact exists.
unsupported_platforms.linux-musl: unsupported because the official Junie linux-* artifact is treated as glibc-bound
unsupported_platforms.unsupported-architecture: Only arm64/aarch64 and x64/amd64 are supported.

runtime_launch.target_environment_scope: T is the explicit control/project root; H is T/.nddev-junie-cli-runtime/home; Junie receives exact target-owned config, guidelines, skills, agents, MCP, commands, hooks, extensions cache, cache, temp, HOME, XDG, data, logs, and JVM home/tmp scopes
runtime_launch.live_home_guard: account ~/.junie metadata must remain unchanged across installer probes and launches
runtime_launch.lock_scope: lifecycle locking acquires a persistent external bootstrap flock first under the resolved fixed system temp root, keyed by the full SHA256 of product namespace plus lexical absolute target before parent/canonical target inspection, then acquires the canonical-target external flock, then acquires the persistent target-internal flock at <target>/.nddev-junie-cli.lock/lock; release order is internal first, canonical external second, lexical external last
runtime_launch.pre_child_artifact_revalidation: target-owned Junie shim and pinned Junie binary path, inode, size, and SHA256 are captured during launch preflight and revalidated immediately before subprocess execution
runtime_launch.verified_path_handoff: macOS does not support this manager executing Junie through fexecve or /dev/fd, so launch retains open verified fds as evidence, materializes a dedicated launch image from the verified target-owned shim at <target>/.nddev-junie-cli-runtime/launch-image/junie, write-protects only that dedicated launcher directory, immediately revalidates identity and digest, then starts the launch image path with Popen
runtime_launch.runtime_state_writable: The managed target, runtime HOME, TMP, XDG, JUNIE_DATA, JUNIE_LOG_DIR, project, and config/source directories are not made read-only by launch handoff protection.
runtime_launch.tamper_boundary: This is a verified-path handoff, not a same-UID sandbox; deliberate same-UID chmod or ancestor replacement outside the dedicated protected lock and launch-image directories remains out of scope.

direct_projection.hooks: hooks/*.py through the managed config loaded by --config-location

local_extension_marketplace.reason: Junie documents local marketplace sources and interactive slash-command installation, but no stable noninteractive install command or deterministic installed-reference id for local sources is documented.
